water.name: Water
water.info: Fresh (sweet) water (H₂O): the universal solvent. Freezes at 0 °C, boils at 100 °C. The sandbox also has Salt Water, which is denser and saltier.

fire.name: Fire
fire.info: Fire: rapid oxidation releasing heat and light. Needs fuel, oxygen and heat.

earth.name: Earth
earth.info: Earth: loose mineral matter — the raw ground beneath us.

air.name: Air
air.info: Air: ~78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen. The mixture we breathe.

energy.name: Energy
energy.info: Energy: the capacity to do work — heat, light, motion, electricity.

heat.name: Heat
heat.info: Heat: thermal energy transferred between bodies at different temperatures.

pressure.name: Pressure
pressure.info: Pressure: force per unit area. Drives phase changes and rock metamorphism.

time.name: Time
time.info: Time: the dimension along which weathering, decay and growth unfold.

electricity.name: Electricity
electricity.info: Electricity: the flow of electric charge through a conductor.

wind.name: Wind
wind.info: Wind: air in motion, driven by pressure differences.

sea.name: Sea
sea.info: Sea: a vast body of salt water covering most of Earth.

steam.name: Steam
steam.info: Steam: water vapour above 100 °C. Condenses back to liquid water on cooling.

lava.name: Lava
lava.info: Lava: molten rock erupted at ~700–1200 °C. Cools into igneous rock.

rain.name: Rain
rain.info: Rain: liquid water droplets falling from clouds.

dust.name: Dust
dust.info: Dust: fine airborne mineral and organic particles.

stone.name: Stone
stone.info: Stone: consolidated rock. The foundation of tools and buildings.

ice.name: Ice
ice.info: Ice: solid water below 0 °C. Less dense than liquid water, so it floats.

cold.name: Cold
cold.info: Cold: low thermal energy. The absence of heat.

frost.name: Frost
frost.info: Frost: ice crystals formed by direct deposition of water vapour.

mist.name: Mist
mist.info: Mist: suspended water droplets near the ground; thin fog.

fog.name: Fog
fog.info: Fog: a dense ground-level cloud of suspended water droplets.

cloud.name: Cloud
cloud.info: Cloud: condensed water droplets or ice crystals suspended in air.

snow.name: Snow
snow.info: Snow: ice crystals that form in clouds and fall as snowflakes.

hail.name: Hail
hail.info: Hail: balls of layered ice formed in strong thunderstorm updrafts.

lightning.name: Lightning
lightning.info: Lightning: a plasma discharge reaching ~30,000 °C — hotter than the Sun's surface.

rainbow.name: Rainbow
rainbow.info: Rainbow: sunlight refracted and dispersed by raindrops into a spectrum.

storm.name: Storm
storm.info: Storm: a disturbed atmosphere with strong wind, rain and often lightning.

light.name: Light
light.info: Light: visible electromagnetic radiation, wavelengths ~400–700 nm.

sun.name: Sun
sun.info: Sun: a G-type star, ~5,500 °C at its surface, fusing hydrogen into helium.

sky.name: Sky
sky.info: Sky: the atmosphere overhead; blue from Rayleigh scattering of sunlight.

laser.name: Laser
laser.info: Laser: coherent, single-wavelength light amplified by stimulated emission.

photon.name: Photon
photon.info: Photon: the quantum (smallest packet) of electromagnetic energy.

hydrogen.name: Hydrogen
hydrogen.info: Hydrogen (H): the lightest, most abundant element. Highly flammable. BP −253 °C.

oxygen.name: Oxygen

reactions.event: Oxygen fed the Fire — it flared up

oxygen.info: Oxygen (O₂): ~21% of air. Supports combustion and respiration. BP −183 °C.

nitrogen.name: Nitrogen
nitrogen.info: Nitrogen (N₂): ~78% of air; inert. Liquid nitrogen boils at −196 °C.

carbon.name: Carbon
carbon.info: Carbon (C): backbone of all life. Forms graphite, diamond and millions of compounds.

sulfur.name: Sulfur
sulfur.info: Sulfur (S): a brittle yellow nonmetal. Burns with a blue flame; melts at 115 °C.

phosphorus.name: Phosphorus
phosphorus.info: Phosphorus (P): white phosphorus ignites in air. Essential to DNA and bone.

silicon.name: Silicon
silicon.info: Silicon (Si): a metalloid and the heart of computer chips. MP 1,414 °C.

sodium.name: Sodium
sodium.info: Sodium (Na): a soft alkali metal that reacts violently with water. MP 98 °C.

chlorine.name: Chlorine
chlorine.info: Chlorine (Cl₂): a toxic green-yellow gas used to disinfect water.

potassium.name: Potassium
potassium.info: Potassium (K): an alkali metal that bursts into lilac flame on water. MP 63 °C.

calcium.name: Calcium
calcium.info: Calcium (Ca): builds bones, shells and limestone. MP 842 °C.

aluminium.name: Aluminium
aluminium.info: Aluminium (Al): light, corrosion-resistant metal. MP 660 °C. Smelted by electrolysis.

iron.name: Iron
iron.info: Iron (Fe): the most-used metal; ferromagnetic. MP 1,538 °C. Rusts in moist air.

copper.name: Copper
copper.info: Copper (Cu): an excellent electrical conductor. MP 1,085 °C.

zinc.name: Zinc
zinc.info: Zinc (Zn): used to galvanise steel against rust. MP 420 °C.

tin.name: Tin
tin.info: Tin (Sn): a soft, low-melting metal smelted from ore, used in solder and bronze. MP 232 °C.

lead.name: Lead
lead.info: Lead (Pb): a heavy, soft, toxic metal once used in pipes and paint. MP 327 °C.

gold.name: Gold
gold.info: Gold (Au): a dense, unreactive precious metal. MP 1,064 °C.

silver.name: Silver
silver.info: Silver (Ag): the best electrical conductor of all metals. MP 962 °C.

nickel.name: Nickel
nickel.info: Nickel (Ni): a ferromagnetic metal used in coins and stainless steel. MP 1,455 °C.

helium.name: Helium
helium.info: Helium (He): an inert noble gas, lighter than air. BP −269 °C, near absolute zero.

gas.name: Gas
gas.info: Gas: a generic gaseous mixture. Air is the ambient background of the sandbox — to test chemistry, paint a SPECIFIC gas (oxygen, methane, chlorine…) instead.

mercury.name: Mercury
mercury.info: Mercury (Hg): the only metal liquid at room temperature. Toxic. BP 357 °C.

cobalt.name: Cobalt
cobalt.info: Cobalt (Co): a ferromagnetic metal; its salts give glass a deep blue.

neodymium.name: Neodymium
neodymium.info: Neodymium (Nd): a rare-earth metal making the strongest permanent magnets.

uranium.name: Uranium
uranium.info: Uranium (U): a dense radioactive metal; fuel for nuclear fission. MP 1,132 °C.

plutonium.name: Plutonium
plutonium.info: Plutonium (Pu): a synthetic radioactive metal used in reactors and weapons.

salt.name: Salt
salt.info: Table salt (NaCl): an ionic crystal. 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl. Melts at 801 °C.

carbon_dioxide.name: Carbon Dioxide
carbon_dioxide.info: Carbon dioxide (CO₂): C + O₂ → CO₂. A greenhouse gas exhaled by animals.

carbon_monoxide.name: Carbon Monoxide
carbon_monoxide.info: Carbon monoxide (CO): a colourless, odourless, deadly gas from incomplete burning.

methane.name: Methane
methane.info: Methane (CH₄): C + 2H₂ → CH₄. The main component of natural gas.

ammonia.name: Ammonia
ammonia.info: Ammonia (NH₃): N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃ (Haber process). Basis of fertiliser.

hydrochloric_acid.name: Hydrochloric Acid
hydrochloric_acid.info: Hydrochloric acid (HCl): a strong acid. H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl. Found in stomach acid.

sulfuric_acid.name: Sulfuric Acid
sulfuric_acid.info: Sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄): the most-produced industrial chemical. Made via the contact process.

sodium_hydroxide.name: Sodium Hydroxide
sodium_hydroxide.info: Sodium hydroxide (NaOH): caustic soda. Made by electrolysis of brine. Used in soap.

limestone.name: Limestone
limestone.info: Limestone (CaCO₃): a sedimentary rock of compressed shells and coral.

quicklime.name: Quicklime
quicklime.info: Quicklime (CaO): CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ when limestone is heated. Used to make cement.

cement.name: Cement
cement.info: Cement: a binder that hardens with water; the glue of concrete.

basalt.name: Basalt
basalt.info: Basalt: a dark, fine-grained igneous rock; the most common volcanic rock.

granite.name: Granite
granite.info: Granite: a coarse, intrusive igneous rock of quartz and feldspar.

sand.name: Sand
sand.info: Sand: weathered rock grains, mostly quartz (SiO₂). Melts into glass at ~1,700 °C.

clay.name: Clay
clay.info: Clay: fine weathered mineral particles; plastic when wet, hard when fired.

sandstone.name: Sandstone
sandstone.info: Sandstone: sedimentary rock formed from cemented sand grains.

marble.name: Marble
marble.info: Marble: metamorphosed limestone, prized by sculptors.

slate.name: Slate
slate.info: Slate: a fine metamorphic rock that splits into flat sheets for roofing.

diamond.name: Diamond
diamond.info: Diamond: pure carbon crystallised under extreme pressure — the hardest natural material.

graphite.name: Graphite
graphite.info: Graphite: soft, layered carbon that conducts electricity — pencil 'lead'.

quartz.name: Quartz
quartz.info: Quartz: crystalline silicon dioxide; piezoelectric and used in watches.

ruby.name: Ruby
ruby.info: Ruby: corundum (Al₂O₃) coloured red by traces of chromium.

coal.name: Coal
coal.info: Coal: a fossil fuel formed from ancient compressed plant matter.

oil.name: Oil
oil.info: Crude oil: a liquid fossil fuel from ancient marine organisms.

gasoline.name: Gasoline
gasoline.info: Gasoline: a volatile fuel distilled from crude oil for engines.

soil.name: Soil
soil.info: Soil: weathered minerals mixed with organic matter; supports plant life.

gravel.name: Gravel
gravel.info: Gravel: loose fragments of rock, larger than sand.

ash.name: Ash
ash.info: Ash: the mineral residue left after combustion.

charcoal.name: Charcoal
charcoal.info: Charcoal: carbon-rich fuel from heating wood without oxygen.

rust.name: Rust
rust.info: Rust (Fe₂O₃): iron oxidised by water and oxygen over time.

steel.name: Steel
steel.info: Steel: iron alloyed with ~0.2–2% carbon — far stronger than pure iron.

stainless_steel.name: Stainless Steel
stainless_steel.info: Stainless steel: steel with chromium and nickel that resists corrosion.

bronze.name: Bronze
bronze.info: Bronze: copper + tin. The defining alloy of the Bronze Age.

brass.name: Brass
brass.info: Brass: copper + zinc. Bright, corrosion-resistant, used for instruments.

glass.name: Glass
glass.info: Glass: silica sand melted at ~1,700 °C and cooled without crystallising.

ceramic.name: Ceramic
ceramic.info: Ceramic: clay hardened by firing in a kiln. Pottery, tiles, porcelain.

brick.name: Brick
brick.info: Brick: a moulded clay block, sun-dried or kiln-fired for building.

concrete.name: Concrete
concrete.info: Concrete: cement + sand + gravel + water — the world's most-used building material.

plastic.name: Plastic
plastic.info: Plastic: synthetic polymers refined from oil; cheap, durable, mouldable.

rubber.name: Rubber
rubber.info: Rubber: an elastic polymer, natural (latex) or synthetic.

silicon_chip.name: Silicon Chip
silicon_chip.info: Silicon chip: a wafer of doped silicon etched with millions of transistors.

graphene.name: Graphene
graphene.info: Graphene: a one-atom-thick sheet of carbon — ultra-strong and conductive.

wood.name: Wood
wood.info: Wood: the fibrous structural tissue of trees; fuel and building material.

brine.name: Brine
brine.info: Brine: highly concentrated salt water; electrolysed to make chlorine and NaOH.

amino_acid.name: Amino Acid
amino_acid.info: Amino acids: the Miller–Urey experiment made these from methane, ammonia and sparks.

protein.name: Protein
protein.info: Protein: long chains of amino acids that fold into life's molecular machines.

cell.name: Cell
cell.info: Cell: the smallest unit of life, bounded by a membrane.

bacteria.name: Bacteria
bacteria.info: Bacteria: single-celled microbes, among the first life on Earth.

algae.name: Algae
algae.info: Algae: simple photosynthetic organisms; early oxygen producers.

plant.name: Plant
plant.info: Plant: a multicellular organism that turns sunlight into sugar.

tree.name: Tree
tree.info: Tree: a tall woody plant; forests are Earth's lungs.

flower.name: Flower
flower.info: Flower: the reproductive structure of flowering plants.

seed.name: Seed
seed.info: Seed: an embryonic plant packaged with a food store.

fish.name: Fish
fish.info: Fish: aquatic vertebrates; the first animals with backbones.

amphibian.name: Amphibian
amphibian.info: Amphibian: vertebrates that bridge water and land, like frogs.

reptile.name: Reptile
reptile.info: Reptile: scaly, egg-laying vertebrates such as lizards and snakes.

dinosaur.name: Dinosaur
dinosaur.info: Dinosaur: dominant land reptiles of the Mesozoic, ancestors of birds.

bird.name: Bird
bird.info: Bird: feathered, warm-blooded descendants of theropod dinosaurs.

mammal.name: Mammal
mammal.info: Mammal: warm-blooded vertebrates with hair that nurse their young.

human.name: Human
human.info: Human (Homo sapiens): a tool-making, language-using primate.

fossil.name: Fossil
fossil.info: Fossil: mineralised remains of ancient life preserved in rock.

sugar.name: Sugar
sugar.info: Sugar (sucrose): a sweet carbohydrate. Caramelises at ~186 °C.

alcohol.name: Alcohol
alcohol.info: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH): made by fermenting sugar with yeast. Boils at 78 °C.

vinegar.name: Vinegar
vinegar.info: Vinegar (acetic acid): ethanol oxidised by bacteria into a mild acid.

yeast.name: Yeast
yeast.info: Yeast: a fungus that ferments sugar into alcohol and CO₂.

dough.name: Dough
dough.info: Dough: flour and water kneaded together — the base of bread.

flour.name: Flour
flour.info: Flour: ground cereal grain, the staple of baking.

bread.name: Bread
bread.info: Bread: leavened dough baked into a staple food.

cheese.name: Cheese
cheese.info: Cheese: milk curdled and aged by bacteria and enzymes.

milk.name: Milk
milk.info: Milk: a nutrient-rich fluid mammals produce to feed their young.

chocolate.name: Chocolate
chocolate.info: Chocolate: cocoa, sugar and milk; melts near body temperature (~34 °C).

syrup.name: Syrup
syrup.info: Syrup: a thick, concentrated sugar solution.

jam.name: Jam
jam.info: Jam: fruit boiled with sugar until it sets.

fruit.name: Fruit
fruit.info: Fruit: the seed-bearing structure of a flowering plant.

wire.name: Wire
wire.info: Wire: a drawn metal strand that carries electric current.

magnet.name: Magnet
magnet.info: Magnet: a material with a persistent magnetic field; iron, nickel and cobalt are ferromagnetic.

generator.name: Generator
generator.info: Generator: spins a magnet past coils to induce electricity (Faraday's law).

battery.name: Battery
battery.info: Battery: stores chemical energy and releases it as electric current.

metal.name: Metal
metal.info: Metal: a lustrous, conductive, malleable material.

acid.name: Acid
acid.info: Acid: a corrosive solution that donates hydrogen ions (low pH).

robot.name: Robot
robot.info: Robot: a programmable machine that senses and acts on the world.

computer.name: Computer
computer.info: Computer: a machine that processes information using logic circuits.

internet.name: Internet
internet.info: Internet: a global network linking billions of computers.

ai.name: Artificial Intelligence
ai.info: AI: software that performs tasks normally requiring human intelligence.

star.name: Star
star.info: Star: a ball of plasma fusing hydrogen into helium, releasing light and heat.

galaxy.name: Galaxy
galaxy.info: Galaxy: billions of stars bound by gravity. Ours is the Milky Way.

supernova.name: Supernova
supernova.info: Supernova: a dying massive star's explosion, forging heavy elements.

black_hole.name: Black Hole
black_hole.info: Black hole: a region where gravity is so strong not even light escapes.

moon.name: Moon
moon.info: Moon: Earth's rocky natural satellite, raising the tides.

planet.name: Planet
planet.info: Planet: a large body orbiting a star, cleared of debris in its path.

space.name: Space
space.info: Space: the near-vacuum beyond a planet's atmosphere.

rocket.name: Rocket
rocket.info: Rocket: a vehicle propelled by ejecting high-speed exhaust — works in vacuum.

nuclear_reactor.name: Nuclear Reactor
nuclear_reactor.info: Nuclear reactor: controls fission of uranium to generate heat and electricity.

nuclear_bomb.name: Nuclear Bomb
nuclear_bomb.info: Nuclear bomb: an uncontrolled chain reaction releasing colossal energy.

fusion.name: Fusion
fusion.info: Fusion: merging light nuclei to release energy — how stars shine.

radiation.name: Radiation
radiation.info: Radiation: energy or particles emitted by unstable (radioactive) atoms.

atom.name: Atom
atom.info: Atom: the smallest unit of an element, a nucleus orbited by electrons.

molecule.name: Molecule
molecule.info: Molecule: two or more atoms bonded together.

electron.name: Electron
electron.info: Electron: a fundamental particle with negative charge; carries electric current.

proton.name: Proton
proton.info: Proton: a positively charged particle in the atomic nucleus.

neutron.name: Neutron
neutron.info: Neutron: a neutral nuclear particle; its count sets the isotope.

quark.name: Quark
quark.info: Quark: a truly fundamental particle; three make a proton or neutron.

plasma.name: Plasma
plasma.info: Plasma: the fourth state of matter — ionised gas, as in stars and lightning.

land.name: Land
land.info: Land: solid ground above the water.

coca_cola.name: Coca Cola
coca_cola.info: Coca Cola: a famous caramel-coloured fizzy drink.

tattoo.name: Tattoo
tattoo.info: Tattoo: ink injected into the skin to make permanent art.

ink.name: Ink
ink.info: Ink: a pigmented liquid used for writing, printing and tattoos.

lady_l.name: Lady L
lady_l.info: Lady L: a legendary icon born of Coca Cola and ink. The crown jewel of CRUCIBLE's secret recipes.

phoenix.name: Phoenix
phoenix.info: Phoenix: a mythical bird reborn from its own ashes.

unicorn.name: Unicorn
unicorn.info: Unicorn: a legendary horse with a single horn.

mermaid.name: Mermaid
mermaid.info: Mermaid: a mythical half-human, half-fish being.

ghost.name: Ghost
ghost.info: Ghost: the spirit of the dead, said to haunt the living.

zombie.name: Zombie
zombie.info: Zombie: a reanimated corpse craving brains.

blood.name: Blood
blood.info: Blood: the red fluid that carries oxygen through the body.

vampire.name: Vampire
vampire.info: Vampire: an undead being that feeds on blood.

werewolf.name: Werewolf
werewolf.info: Werewolf: a human that transforms under the full moon.

golem.name: Golem
golem.info: Golem: a creature of clay brought to life by magic.

wizard.name: Wizard
wizard.info: Wizard: a wielder of arcane magic.

potion.name: Potion
potion.info: Potion: a magical brew with mysterious effects.

crystal_ball.name: Crystal Ball
crystal_ball.info: Crystal ball: a sphere said to reveal the future.

excalibur.name: Excalibur
excalibur.info: Excalibur: the legendary sword of King Arthur.

genie.name: Genie
genie.info: Genie: a wish-granting spirit of myth.

fairy.name: Fairy
fairy.info: Fairy: a tiny winged magical being.

kraken.name: Kraken
kraken.info: Kraken: a giant sea monster of Norse legend.

yeti.name: Yeti
yeti.info: Yeti: an ape-like creature of the Himalayan snows.

ninja.name: Ninja
ninja.info: Ninja: a stealthy covert agent of feudal Japan.

samurai.name: Samurai
samurai.info: Samurai: an elite warrior of old Japan.

robot_army.name: Robot Army
robot_army.info: Robot army: a legion of machines.

meme.name: Meme
meme.info: Meme: an idea that spreads across the internet.

troll.name: Troll
troll.info: Troll: a cave-dwelling brute — or an internet pest.

emoji.name: Emoji
emoji.info: Emoji: a tiny pictogram used in messages.

god.name: God
god.info: God: a supreme being of myth and faith.

philosophers_stone.name: Philosopher's Stone
philosophers_stone.info: Philosopher's Stone: the legendary alchemical substance that turns lead to gold.

gold_from_lead.name: Alchemic Gold
gold_from_lead.info: Gold transmuted from lead — the alchemist's dream realised.

rave.name: Rave
rave.info: Rave: an all-night electronic dance party.

techno.name: Techno
techno.info: Techno: pounding electronic dance music born in Detroit.

machine.name: Machine
machine.info: Machine: a device that does work using power.

hard_techno.name: Hard Techno
hard_techno.info: Hard Techno: relentless, high-BPM industrial techno.

coffee.name: Coffee
coffee.info: Coffee: a caffeinated brew that fuels the world.

pizza.name: Pizza
pizza.info: Pizza: baked dough with toppings — Italy's gift to the world.

wave.name: Wave
wave.info: Wave: energy travelling across the surface of water.

tsunami.name: Tsunami
tsunami.info: Tsunami: a giant sea wave triggered by an undersea quake.

earthquake.name: Earthquake
earthquake.info: Earthquake: ground shaking from sudden movement of tectonic plates.

volcano.name: Volcano
volcano.info: Volcano: a vent where molten rock erupts onto the surface.

tornado.name: Tornado
tornado.info: Tornado: a violently rotating column of air touching the ground.

hurricane.name: Hurricane
hurricane.info: Hurricane: a vast rotating tropical storm system.

flame.name: Flame
flame.info: Flame: the visible glowing region of a fire — the fire triangle needs fuel, heat and oxygen.

forest.name: Forest
forest.info: Forest: a dense community of trees.

wildfire.name: Wildfire
wildfire.info: Wildfire: an uncontrolled fire spreading through vegetation.

swamp.name: Swamp
swamp.info: Swamp: a forested wetland of slow water and mud.

desert.name: Desert
desert.info: Desert: an arid region receiving little rain.

glacier.name: Glacier
glacier.info: Glacier: a slow-moving river of compacted ice.

dune.name: Dune
dune.info: Dune: a hill of wind-blown sand.

element_lithium.name: Lithium
element_lithium.info: Lithium: the lightest metal, used in batteries.

element_beryllium.name: Beryllium
element_beryllium.info: Beryllium: a light, stiff, toxic metal.

element_boron.name: Boron
element_boron.info: Boron: a metalloid used in glass and detergents.

element_fluorine.name: Fluorine
element_fluorine.info: Fluorine: the most reactive element, a pale gas.

element_neon.name: Neon
element_neon.info: Neon: a noble gas that glows orange-red in lights.

element_sodium.name: Sodium
element_sodium.info: Sodium: a soft, reactive metal; half of table salt.

element_magnesium.name: Magnesium
element_magnesium.info: Magnesium: a light metal that burns bright white.

element_silicon.name: Silicon
element_silicon.info: Silicon: the semiconductor at the heart of chips.

element_phosphorus.name: Phosphorus
element_phosphorus.info: Phosphorus: glows in the dark; vital to life.

element_chlorine.name: Chlorine
element_chlorine.info: Chlorine: a green, toxic gas used to disinfect water.

element_argon.name: Argon
element_argon.info: Argon: an inert noble gas filling light bulbs.

element_potassium.name: Potassium
element_potassium.info: Potassium: a reactive metal essential to nerves.

element_calcium.name: Calcium
element_calcium.info: Calcium: builds bones, shells and limestone.

element_chromium.name: Chromium
element_chromium.info: Chromium: a hard, shiny metal used in plating.

element_cobalt.name: Cobalt
element_cobalt.info: Cobalt: a magnetic metal used in blue pigments.

element_nickel.name: Nickel
element_nickel.info: Nickel: a tough metal used in coins and alloys.

element_krypton.name: Krypton
element_krypton.info: Krypton: a noble gas used in some lighting.

element_tin.name: Tin
element_tin.info: Tin: a soft metal used to coat cans and make solder.

element_iodine.name: Iodine
element_iodine.info: Iodine: a purple-black solid used as antiseptic.

element_xenon.name: Xenon
element_xenon.info: Xenon: a heavy noble gas used in bright lamps.

element_platinum.name: Platinum
element_platinum.info: Platinum: a dense, precious, unreactive metal.

element_mercury.name: Mercury
element_mercury.info: Mercury: the only metal liquid at room temperature.

element_lead.name: Lead
element_lead.info: Lead: a heavy, soft, toxic metal.

element_uranium.name: Uranium
element_uranium.info: Uranium: a radioactive metal that fuels reactors.

element_plutonium.name: Plutonium
element_plutonium.info: Plutonium: a radioactive metal used in weapons.

element_tungsten.name: Tungsten
element_tungsten.info: Tungsten: highest melting point of all metals.

element_helium_e.name: Helium
element_helium_e.info: Helium: a light noble gas that lifts balloons.

nitric_acid.name: Nitric Acid
nitric_acid.info: Nitric acid: a strong acid used in fertilisers and explosives.

baking_soda.name: Baking Soda
baking_soda.info: Baking soda: leavens cakes and neutralises acids.

hydrogen_peroxide.name: Hydrogen Peroxide
hydrogen_peroxide.info: Hydrogen peroxide: a bleaching, disinfecting liquid.

ozone.name: Ozone
ozone.info: Ozone: a reactive form of oxygen that shields us from UV.

ethanol.name: Ethanol
ethanol.info: Ethanol: drinking alcohol and a clean-burning fuel.

methanol.name: Methanol
methanol.info: Methanol: wood alcohol, toxic but useful as fuel.

acetone.name: Acetone
acetone.info: Acetone: a solvent and nail-polish remover.

glucose.name: Glucose
glucose.info: Glucose: the sugar that fuels living cells.

calcium_carbonate.name: Calcium Carbonate
calcium_carbonate.info: Calcium carbonate: chalk, limestone and seashells.

silicon_dioxide.name: Silicon Dioxide
silicon_dioxide.info: Silicon dioxide: quartz and the main component of sand.

dry_ice.name: Dry Ice
dry_ice.info: Dry ice: frozen carbon dioxide that sublimes into fog.

animal.name: Animal
animal.info: Animal: a multicellular organism that moves and feeds.

insect.name: Insect
insect.info: Insect: a six-legged arthropod — the most numerous animals.

cow.name: Cow
cow.info: Cow: a domesticated bovine raised for milk and beef.

horse.name: Horse
horse.info: Horse: a hooved mammal long used for transport.

pig.name: Pig
pig.info: Pig: an intelligent farm animal raised for pork.

lion.name: Lion
lion.info: Lion: the social big cat of the savanna.

tiger.name: Tiger
